interview.hardest_part: Navigating the hotel interior with arrow-key turning and half-second key holds: doors, stairs, the elevator, and the ground floor to the safe room require precise heading control, and small misalignments compound into getting stuck in corners or wandering off the route.
interview.likely_failure: Getting stuck on geometry or a closed door while the AI teammates move ahead, then being swarmed by a horde or a special infected (Smoker/Charger/Hunter) while facing the wrong direction — losing route progress milestones is the biggest risk, since route milestones are worth roughly half the points.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Easy difficulty means low incoming damage and weak commons; three AI teammates handle most killing and revives, and I can follow them as a moving waypoint. Linear, corridor-like level design with visible objective markers, generous ammo, and milestones rewarding distance plus kills/shots/time all accumulate passively as long as I keep moving forward.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Only arrow keys for looking means no reliable precision aiming or quick 180-degree turns; discrete half-second inputs make fine positioning and doorway threading difficult. Pinning against walls, door-use prompts needing exact crosshair placement, special infected grabs that need instant response, and the 3-hour wall-clock limit that punishes slow deliberation all work against me.
